- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.3) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope or add 2–5% upward bias in second half of horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, avoid downward push unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to ignore them; apply a 2–4% upward correction to offset sentiment-induced underreaction.
